scope: capability fixtures only; four original command gaps remain open

selection.context: For f004 and f007, the question presupposes that a bare command obligates absent an admissible qarina; no other command-default position is modeled.

original_case.note: Whether writing or gesture counts as a command (al-Qadi: not truly; his Jami' argument from the Prophet's letters implies it does) is a question about what constitutes the command, prior to and outside the kernel, which presupposes a command and only assigns its status.

Whether the Prophet's act is called a command literally (Abu al-Barakat: only figuratively, per Ahmad and the majority; some Malikis/Shafi'is and Abu Ya'la's Kifaya: literally) is governed by the theory of the Prophet's acts and the semantics of the word 'amr', not by the bare-command default.

Whether an unqualified threat, or the words 'obligatory'/'fard', are a text (nass) for obligation that admits no reinterpretation (al-Qadi: no; Abu al-Barakat, preferred: yes) asks whether an indication may override the default at all, whereas the kernel lets any qarina override every command.

Once nadb (or ibaha) is meant by the command the status is not in dispute; the dispute (literal per Ahmad's apparent words, al-Qadi and most companions vs figurative per al-Karkhi, al-Razi and al-Halwani; for ibaha Abu al-Barakat and Ibn 'Aqil say figurative) is over literal vs figurative usage, which the kernel does not model.

review_questions.question: Can the writing inference be used beyond writing, especially for gesture? No positive gesture conclusion is encoded without a transmitted attestation.
What establishes imitation of the Prophet's act in an application, and how does literal naming relate to an act's ruling? The author's conditional inference is preserved.
Which indications are admissible for the three explicit obligation expressions under each reported reading? Neither a case-specific indication nor an adopted reading is selected.
How should the conflicting al-Qadi permission reports be reconciled under the question's stated command position? Literal or figurative naming must not change the given intended ruling.
